title: Encore of Episode 32: The Scientific Process

sentences.en: Researchers recently tried to replicate a hundred experiments in psychology.
sentences.zh: 研究人员最近尝试重复了一百项心理学实验。

sentences.en: The Center for Open Science recruited colleagues from around the world to try and replicate a hundred studies.
sentences.zh: 开放科学中心招募了来自世界各地的同行，尝试重复一百项研究。

sentences.en: And found that most of them could not be reproduced with the same results.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，其中大多数研究无法通过相同的结果重现。

sentences.en: Today we're going to talk about what has been called a replication crisis in science.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要聊聊科学界被称为“复制危机”的现象。

sentences.en: The replicators in this recent study failed to get the same findings from the original experiment.
sentences.zh: 这项最新研究中的复制者未能从原始实验中得出相同的发现。

sentences.en: From cancer medicine to psychology, researchers are finding that many claims made in scientific studies
sentences.zh: 从癌症医学到心理学，研究人员发现科学研究中提出的许多说法

sentences.en: fail to hold up when those studies are repeated by an independent group.
sentences.zh: 当这些研究由独立小组重复时，往往经不起推验。

sentences.en: Later in this episode, we're going to explore one provocative study
sentences.zh: 在本期节目的后面，我们将探讨一项引人深思的研究

sentences.en: that looked at stereotypes about Asians, women, and math tests
sentences.zh: 该研究探讨了关于亚洲人、女性和数学测试的刻板印象

sentences.en: and explained what happened when researchers tried to reproduce the finding.
sentences.zh: 并解释了当研究人员试图重现这一发现时发生了什么。

sentences.en: We're going to use this story to explore a deeper question.
sentences.zh: 我们将通过这个故事来探讨一个更深层次的问题。

sentences.en: What do scientists really mean when they talk about the truth?
sentences.zh: 科学家在谈论真理时，真正的意思是什么？

sentences.en: Let's take a moment to thank and share a message from our sponsor, LearnVeSt.
sentences.zh: 让我们花点时间感谢并分享赞助商 LearnVest 的一条信息。

sentences.en: LearnVest is an online financial advice company focused on empowering people nationwide
sentences.zh: LearnVest 是一家在线财务咨询公司，致力于帮助全国各地的人们

sentences.en: to make good decisions with their money.
Studies show that writing down your goals makes you 49% more likely to achieve them.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，写下你的目标会使你实现目标的可能性增加 49%。

sentences.en: That's why when you work with LearnVest, you tell them what you want to accomplish,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当你与 LearnVest 合作时，你告诉他们你想完成什么，

sentences.en: and they create a customized financial plan to help you get there.
sentences.zh: 他们会为你制定量身定制的财务计划来帮助你达成目标。

sentences.en: Plus, they pair you with a financial planner to help keep you on track.
sentences.zh: 此外，他们还会为你配对一名理财规划师，帮助你保持进度。

sentences.en: To see a sample plan and get a $50 credit, go to learnveSt.com slash brain.
sentences.zh: 要查看示例计划并获得 50 美元信用额度，请访问 learnvest.com/brain。

sentences.en: The crisis has actually been a long time coming.
sentences.zh: 这场危机其实由来已久。

sentences.en: In 2011, for example, Dutch researchers claimed that broken sidewalks encourage racism.
sentences.zh: 例如，在 2011 年，荷兰研究人员声称破损的人行道会助长种族主义。

sentences.en: They published their findings in one of the most prestigious academic journals, Science Magazine.
sentences.zh: 他们在最负盛名的学术期刊之一《科学》杂志上发表了他们的发现。

sentences.en: A couple of years later, another article in Science showed that when a gay person shows up at a stranger's door
sentences.zh: 几年后，《科学》杂志上的另一篇文章表明，当同性恋者出现在陌生人家门口

sentences.en: and speaks openly about what it's like to be gay, this has an extraordinary effect.
sentences.zh: 并公开谈论身为同性恋的感受时，这会产生非凡的效果。

sentences.en: It was the personal connection between the gay person who they were trying to show, you know, they're in person.
sentences.zh: 这是同性恋者与他们试图展示的人之间的个人联系，你知道的，他们是面谈的。

sentences.en: People who are against gay marriage change their minds after these emotional encounters.
sentences.zh: 反对同性婚姻的人在经历这些情感碰撞后改变了主意。

sentences.en: It was the combination of, you know, contact with a minority coupled with a discussion of issues pertinent.
sentences.zh: 这是你知道的与少数群体接触结合对相关问题的讨论的结果。

sentences.en: The results were written up in the New York Times, the Wall Street Journal, the Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 这些结果被《纽约时报》、《华尔街日报》、《华盛顿邮报》报道。

sentences.en: They were featured on public radio programs, such as the clip you're hearing on Science Friday.
sentences.zh: 它们被公共广播节目特色报道，例如你正在《科学星期五》节目中听到的片段。

sentences.en: Finally, in 2009, researchers claimed that bilingualism, the ability to speak more than one language, is better for your brain.
sentences.zh: 最后，在 2009 年，研究人员声称双语能力，即说一种以上语言的能力，对你的大脑更好。

sentences.en: All these claims had serious probleMs.
sentences.zh: 所有这些说法都有严重的问题。

sentences.en: The Dutch claim was based on fabricated data.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人的说法是基于篡改的数据。

sentences.en: One author of the gay marriage claim asked for the paper to be withdrawn after concerns were raised about fraud.
sentences.zh: 同性恋婚姻说法的其中一位作者在人们对欺诈产生担忧后要求撤回论文。
这两种说法都被撤回了。

sentences.en: Because it turns out the researchers made up the data.
sentences.zh: 因为事实证明研究人员捏造了数据。

sentences.en: The bilingual advantage paper wasn't fabricated, but it was missing important context.
sentences.zh: 双语优势论文没有被捏造，但它缺少重要的背景。

sentences.en: The researchers had conducted four experiments.
sentences.zh: 研究人员进行了四项实验。

sentences.en: Three failed to show that bilingualism was better for the brain.
sentences.zh: 其中三项未能表明双语对大脑更好。

sentences.en: Only one experiment showed a benefit.
sentences.zh: 只有一项实验显示出益处。

sentences.en: It was the only one that was published.
Angela de Brown was on the team that worked on the bilingual advantage study.
sentences.zh: 安吉拉·德布朗是参与双语优势研究团队的一员。

sentences.en: It is troubling because we like to believe that what we see is actually the truth.
sentences.zh: 这令人不安，因为我们愿意相信我们看到的就是事实。

sentences.en: But if it's only half of the results we find and we're, in effect, hiding the other half of the results,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们发现的只是结果的一半，而实际上我们隐藏了结果的另一半，

sentences.en: then we will never really find out what's going on.
sentences.zh: 那么我们就永远无法真正弄清楚到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: At the University of Virginia, psychologist Brian Nozick decided something had to be done.
sentences.zh: 在弗吉尼亚大学，心理学家布赖恩·诺齐克决定必须采取行动。

sentences.en: Brian felt the problem was that too many researchers and too many scientific journals
sentences.zh: 布赖恩觉得问题在于太多研究人员和太多科学期刊

sentences.en: were focusing on publishing new and unusual findings.
sentences.zh: 过于专注于发表新的和不同寻常的发现。

sentences.en: Too few were spending time cross-checking earlier work to make sure it was solid.
sentences.zh: 花时间交叉检查早期工作以确保其扎实的人太少了。

sentences.en: One of the key factors of science is that a claim becomes a credible claim by being reproducible.
sentences.zh: 科学的关键因素之一是，一个主张通过可重现性成为一个可信的主张。

sentences.en: That someone else can take the same approach, the same protocol, the same procedure,
sentences.zh: 即其他人可以采用相同的方法、相同的方案、相同的程序，

sentences.en: do it again themselves, and obtain a similar result.
sentences.zh: 自己再做一次，并获得类似的结果。

sentences.en: Brian launched an effort to reproduce dozens of studies in psychology.
sentences.zh: 布赖恩发起了一项重现数十项心理学研究的努力。
他在 2015 年发表了一份报告。

sentences.en: We found that we were able to reproduce the original results in less than half of the cases
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在评估复制成功与否的五项不同标准中，

sentences.en: across five different criteria of evaluating whether a replication was successful or not.
sentences.zh: 我们在不到一半的案例中能够重现原始结果。

sentences.en: Over the last year, there have been many debates about what this means.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，关于这意味着什么有很多争论。

sentences.en: Some critics say it proves that most studies are worthless.
sentences.zh: 一些批评者说这证明了大多数研究都是毫无价值的。

sentences.en: At many universities, researchers feel it's their integrity,
sentences.zh: 在许多大学里，研究人员觉得他们的正直，

sentences.en: not just their scientific conclusions, that are being called into question.
sentences.zh: 而不仅仅是他们的科学结论，正在受到质疑。

sentences.en: At Harvard University, psychologist Dan Gilbert recently published a paper
sentences.zh: 在哈佛大学，心理学家丹·吉尔伯特最近发表了一篇论文
对布赖恩的结论提出了质疑。

sentences.en: So I think we just have to use our heads to figure out which kinds of things we expect to replicate directly
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们只需要动脑筋弄清楚我们期望哪些类型的事情直接复制

sentences.en: and which kinds of things we would only expect a conceptual replication.
sentences.zh: 以及我们只期望概念复制哪些类型的事情。

sentences.en: And we need to calm down when we don't see direct replication
sentences.zh: 当我们看不到直接复制时，我们需要冷静下来

sentences.en: and ask whether we really should have expected it all.
sentences.zh: 并问问我们是否真的应该预料到这一切。

sentences.en: To unpack all of this, let's take a detailed look at one study
sentences.zh: 为了剖析所有这些，让我们详细看看一项研究

sentences.en: and what happened when researchers tried to replicate it.
sentences.zh: 以及研究人员试图复制它时发生了什么。

sentences.en: I think the story reveals many truths about the ongoing controversy.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个故事揭示了关于正在进行的争议的许多真相。

sentences.en: When they were graduate students at Harvard,
sentences.zh: 当他们在哈佛大学读研究生时，

sentences.en: Todd Patinsky and his friend Margaret Shee often went to restaurants together.
sentences.zh: 托德·帕廷斯基和他的朋友玛格丽特·希经常一起去餐馆。

sentences.en: They went for the food, but they also spent a lot of time observing human behavior.
sentences.zh: 他们是为了食物而去，但也花了很多时间观察人类行为。

sentences.en: We often, after class, would go to the Cheesecake Factory
sentences.zh: 我们经常在课后去芝乐坊餐厅，

sentences.en: and she would order a strawberry shortcake
sentences.zh: 她会点一份草莓短蛋糕，

sentences.en: and I would typically order a salad
sentences.zh: 而我通常会点一份沙拉，

sentences.en: and the number of times that the salad was delivered to her
sentences.zh: 沙拉送到她面前的次数

sentences.en: and the strawberry shortcake was delivered to me.
sentences.zh: 和草莓短蛋糕送到我面前的次数...

sentences.en: She also likes regular Coke and I'm a diabetic, so I drink Diet Coke.
sentences.zh: 她还喜欢普通可乐，而我是个糖尿病患者，所以我喝健怡可乐。

sentences.en: And without fail, the Diet Coke would go to her and the regular Coke would go to me.
sentences.zh: 而且每次健怡可乐都会端给她，普通可乐会端给我。

sentences.en: The waiters were stereotyping Todd and Margaret.
sentences.zh: 服务员对托德和玛格丽特进行了刻板印象的划分。

sentences.en: The guy was probably ordering the less healthy stuff.
sentences.zh: 那家伙可能在点不太健康的东西。

sentences.en: The woman was ordering salads and diet drinks.
sentences.zh: 这个女人在点沙拉和减肥饮料。

sentences.en: Todd and Margaret knew there was lots of research into the effects of such stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 托德和玛格丽特知道有大量关于这种刻板印象影响的研究。

sentences.en: Now, getting a dish you haven't ordered is one thing,
sentences.zh: 现在，拿到一盘你没点过的菜是一回事，

sentences.en: but there are more serious consequences.
But as Todd and Margaret observed the waiters,
sentences.zh: 但正当托德和玛格丽特观察服务员时，

sentences.en: they realized something was missing in the research.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到研究中缺少了一些东西。

sentences.en: The previous studies had focused on the negative consequences of stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 先前的研究集中在刻板印象的负面后果上。

sentences.en: Could stereotypes also work in a positive fashion?
sentences.zh: 刻板印象也能以积极的方式起作用吗？

sentences.en: We thought if we really want to understand how stereotypes operate in the world,
sentences.zh: 我们认为，如果我们真的想了解刻板印象在世界上是如何运作的，

sentences.en: we can't simply look at half of it.
The young researchers brainstormed how they might study the other half of the equation.
sentences.zh: 这两位年轻的研究人员集思广益，探讨他们如何研究方程式的另一半。

sentences.en: The answer came to them as they were, yeah, eating together.
sentences.zh: 当他们在一起吃冰淇淋时，答案浮现了，是的。

sentences.en: We were sitting in Harvard Square over ice cream
sentences.zh: 我们坐在哈佛广场吃冰淇淋，

sentences.en: and we said what we need is a group where the stereotypes go in very different directions.
sentences.zh: 我们说我们需要一个刻板印象走向截然不同的群体。

sentences.en: They wanted to study a situation where stereotypes could have both positive and negative effects.
sentences.zh: 他们想研究刻板印象既有积极影响又有消极影响的情况。

sentences.en: And Margaret, she happens to be an Asian American and a woman
sentences.zh: 而玛格丽特碰巧是一位亚裔美国女性，

sentences.en: and we started talking about math identities
sentences.zh: 我们开始谈论数学认同，

sentences.en: and we kept going back and forth and back and forth
sentences.zh: 我们不断地来回讨论，来回讨论，

sentences.en: and then literally at the same moment we said,
sentences.zh: 然后字面意思上在同一时刻我们说，

sentences.en: well, why don't we study Asian women in math?
sentences.zh: 嗯，为什么我们不研究数学中的亚洲女性呢？

sentences.en: The experiment they designed was ingenious and simple.
sentences.zh: 他们设计的实验巧妙而简单。

sentences.en: There are negative stereotypes about women doing math
sentences.zh: 关于女性学数学存在负面刻板印象，

sentences.en: and positive stereotypes about Asians in math.
sentences.zh: 而关于亚洲人学数学存在正面刻板印象。

sentences.en: So what happens when you give a math test to women who are Asian?
sentences.zh: 那么，当你给擅长数学的女性进行数学测试时会发生什么？

sentences.en: We hypothesize that when you make different identities salient,
sentences.zh: 我们假设，当你使不同的认同凸显时，

sentences.en: you should expect different stereotypes to be applied.
sentences.zh: 你应该期望应用不同的刻板印象。

sentences.en: Todd and Margaret figured that if they reminded Asian women about their gender,
sentences.zh: 托德和玛格丽特认为，如果他们提醒亚洲女性注意她们的性别，

sentences.en: they would see the negative stereotype at work.
sentences.zh: 他们就会看到负面的刻板印象在起作用。

sentences.en: But what would happen if they subtly reminded the volunteers about their Asian identity?
sentences.zh: 但如果他们巧妙地提醒志愿者注意她们的亚洲身份会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: The researchers recruited Asian women as volunteers
sentences.zh: 研究人员招募了亚洲女性作为志愿者，

sentences.en: and asked some of them to identify their gender on a form before taking a math teSt.
sentences.zh: 并要求其中一些人在参加数学测试前在表格上标明她们的性别。

sentences.en: Earlier research had shown that when you make gender salient in this way,
sentences.zh: 先前的研究表明，当你以这种方式凸显性别时，

sentences.en: this triggers the negative stereotype about women in math.
sentences.zh: 这会触发关于女性学数学的负面刻板印象。

sentences.en: Todd and Margaret reminded other volunteers selected at random about their Asian heritage.
sentences.zh: 托德和玛格丽特提醒随机挑选的其他志愿者注意她们的亚洲血统。

sentences.en: They wanted to make these volunteers remember the stereotype about Asians being good at math.
sentences.zh: 他们想让这些志愿者记住关于亚洲人擅长数学的刻板印象。

sentences.en: After all the volunteers finished the tests, the researchers analyzed their performance.
sentences.zh: 所有志愿者完成测试后，研究人员分析了他们的表现。

sentences.en: Todd was working down the hall from Margaret one day when he heard her call out to him.
sentences.zh: 一天，托德正在玛格丽特办公室大厅对面的走廊工作，听到她大声叫他。

sentences.en: She just shouted, holy cow, it worked.
sentences.zh: 她只是大喊，天哪，成功了。

sentences.en: So I just sort of ran down there and we started looking at the output together.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是跑过去，我们开始一起看输出结果。

sentences.en: The study found that when the volunteers were reminded that they were women,
sentences.zh: 研究发现，当提醒志愿者她们是女性时，

sentences.en: they did worse on the math teSt.
sentences.zh: 她们在数学测试中表现更差。

sentences.en: When they were reminded that they were Asian, they did better.
sentences.zh: 当提醒她们是亚洲人时，她们表现得更好。
同样的女性，同样的数学测试。
负面刻板印象，负面结果。
正面刻板印象，正面结果。

sentences.en: The study was an instant sensation.

sentences.zh: 心理学家布赖恩·诺齐克。

sentences.en: This is one of my favorite effects in psychological science.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的心理科学效应之一。

sentences.en: Something that seems like it shouldn't be flexible, how well we perform in math,
sentences.zh: 看起来不应该灵活的事情，我们在数学上表现得有多好，

sentences.en: is flexible as a function of the identities that we have in mind
sentences.zh: 作为我们脑海中的认同和与这些认同相关的刻板印象的函数是灵活的。

sentences.en: and stereotypes associated with those identities.
sentences.zh: 亚洲人擅长数学，女性不那么擅长数学。

sentences.en: Asians being good at math, women being not as good at math.
sentences.zh: 心理学家卡罗琳·吉布森说，这项研究迅速成为大学教科书的主打内容。

sentences.en: The study quickly became a staple of college textbooks, says psychologist Carolyn Gibson.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当惊人的发现。

sentences.en: It is a pretty amazing finding.
sentences.zh: 我作为本科生第一次听说那项研究。

sentences.en: And I heard about that study for the first time as an undergrad.
sentences.zh: 四年多来，它一直被用作社会心理学课程中的一个例子，

sentences.en: It's been used as an example in social psychology courses for four years,
sentences.zh: 自从它于 1999 年发表以来。
它被用作刻板印象威胁和刻板印象助推的好例子。

sentences.en: And it's used as a good example for stereotype threat and stereotype booSt.
sentences.zh: 但从科学角度来看，有一个大问题。

sentences.en: But from a scientific perspective, there was one big problem.
It had never been replicated exactly.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人遵循他们遵循的步骤并复制他们的结果。

sentences.en: Somebody had never followed their steps that they followed and replicated their results.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人遵循他们遵循的步骤并复制他们的结果。

sentences.en: But it's been used to support further studies many times over the past 15 years.
sentences.zh: 但在过去15年里，它多次被用来支持进一步的研究。
布莱恩·诺齐克表示赞同。

sentences.en: Someone needed to replicate the original study.
sentences.zh: 有人需要重复最初的研究。

sentences.en: He was spearheading a mammoth effort to reproduce dozens of studies in psychology.
sentences.zh: 他当时正带头开展一项庞大的工作，试图重现几十项心理学研究。

sentences.en: Along with a panel of reviewers, he selected this study for replication
sentences.zh: 在评审小组的协助下，他挑选了这项研究进行重复验证，

sentences.en: and asked Carolyn Gibson at Georgia Southern University to conduct it.
sentences.zh: 并邀请佐治亚南方大学的卡罗琳·吉布森来实施。

sentences.en: Brian wanted the replication to closely match the conditions of the original study.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩希望重复实验能尽可能贴近原研究的条件。

sentences.en: If you don't do that, you really are conducting two different studies.
sentences.zh: 如果你不这样做，你实际上就是在做两个完全不同的研究。

sentences.en: After launching the replication, he had second thoughts about its location in the South.
sentences.zh: 启动重复实验后，他对将其地点设在南方产生了疑虑。

sentences.en: And the reviewers thought, this looks like a case where the location might matter.
